items.title: SHAPE-SSA is published in Communications Earth & Environment
items.summary: Our region-specific soil health assessment protocol for Sub-Saharan Africa is now out, the first chapter of my dissertation in print.
items.body:
Soil health scores only mean something when they are compared against soils that could realistically be similar. SHAPE-SSA benchmarks soil organic carbon against the climate, soil type, and management context it comes from, instead of one fixed threshold for a whole continent.

The paper is open access in Communications Earth & Environment and is the work of a team spanning the University of Florida, CIMMYT, and partners in Ethiopia. Thank you to every co-author.

items.title: Presenting, moderating, and judging at CANVAS 2025
items.summary: In Salt Lake City I presented our minimum interpretable predictor set, moderated a soil carbon session, and judged student talks.
items.body:
At the ASA-CSSA-SSSA Annual Meeting (CANVAS 2025) I presented a minimum interpretable predictor set and region-specific framework for scalable soil health assessment.

I also moderated Session 202, Soil Carbon Farming as a Climate Change Solution, and served as a judge for the student oral presentation competition.

items.title: Fall field sampling in Florida
items.summary: Out with lab mates collecting soil samples across Florida cropping and cover crop systems.
items.body: Field days are where the data starts. This fall we sampled soils under cover crops and production fields in Florida as part of the Sustainable Tropical Soil Management Lab's work on soil health in sandy soils.

items.title: Interpretable minimum predictor set for soil carbon mapping published
items.summary: Our robust rank aggregation approach to choosing fewer, better predictors for soil organic carbon mapping is out in Computers and Electronics in Agriculture.
items.body: Digital soil maps often use hundreds of environmental covariates. We showed that a small, interpretable set chosen by robust rank aggregation can map soil organic carbon reliably with far fewer inputs, which makes models easier to explain and to scale.

items.title: SHAPE-SSA poster at the UF Water Institute Symposium
items.summary: I presented SHAPE-SSA at the 10th Biennial Water Institute Symposium in Gainesville.
items.body: A good poster session is a two-hour conversation. Thanks to everyone who stopped by to talk about context-specific soil health benchmarks.

items.title: Sharing our soil health framework at the South Florida symposium
items.summary: I presented our soil health assessment framework at the 8th Annual South Florida graduate research symposium.
items.body: I presented our ongoing work on a soil health assessment framework that supports sustainable agriculture and better land management. Grateful for the feedback and the conversations.
